key_insight: Universal quantum state purification has a direct resource tradeoff: achieving higher fidelity requires a quantifiable amount of magic, captured exactly by a linear mana law in odd dimensions and by linear robustness bounds for qubits.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum error-mitigation and fault-tolerant protocol designers a concrete rule for how much nonstabilizer resource is needed to boost state fidelity at a given success probability.
method: Prove an exact linear mana law for two-copy universal purification in odd dimensions.
Derive two-sided linear robustness bounds for multi-qubit systems, exact for a single qubit.
Construct an explicit successful purification map to expose the fidelity–magic tradeoff.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical theorems and an explicit protocol, rather than numerical benchmarking or experimental data, to establish the purification-resource laws.
watch_item: The results are for universal purification with two input copies, so direct applicability to larger-copy or hardware-constrained settings may require additional analysis.
paper_title: A Nonstabilizerness Resource Law for Universal Quantum State Purification
